drafts.title: Keep or improve ride comfort on broken pavement
drafts.description: Passengers experience a smooth, composed ride on broken pavement and pothole-ridden surfaces; the car should not feel harsh or jarring on typical worn roads.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In a user trial on a standardized 10 km broken-pavement route (mixed potholes and cracks, average roughness matching urban B-level roads), at least 80% of participants rate ride comfort >= 4 out of 5 and measured seat-acceleration RMS does not exceed 0.7 m/s² averaged across trials.
assumptions: Standardized broken-pavement route defined by validation team and repeatable across test labs.
Suspension hardware and control updates within successor vehicle scope.
Ride perception target (4/5) aligns with current BMW 5 Series customer expectations.
uncertainties: Trade-offs with sporty handling at limits may require tuning choices prioritized by trim level.
Performance may vary with wheel/tire packages; tests assume production-standard tires.

drafts.title: Reduce distracting wind noise at highway speeds
drafts.description: At highway speeds, exterior aerodynamic noise should not be perceived as distracting by occupants so long highway trips remain comfortable.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: On a defined highway route at 75 mph (120 km/h), in a user trial fewer than 10% of participants report wind noise as 'distracting' and interior aero-noise contribution does not increase participant annoyance score by more than 1 point on a 7-point scale compared with baseline quiet reference.
assumptions: Tests run with production-spec windows closed and standard exterior mirrors.
Reference annoyance scores established from existing benchmark vehicles.
uncertainties: Roof-rack or aftermarket accessories will change aero behavior and are excluded from tests.
Perception varies with passenger hearing sensitivity and road surface; test cohort should be representative.

drafts.title: Make lane-keeping assist smooth and predictable in curves
drafts.description: Lane-keeping interventions steer smoothly through curves without abrupt corrections so occupants feel confident and comfortable when the feature is active.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: On a standardized series of curved-road tests (multiple radii, moderate superelevation), 90% of lane-keeping assist events produce lateral-jerk values below 0.12 m/s³ and at least 95% of test drivers rate lateral control smoothness >= 4 out of 5.
assumptions: Standardized curved-road test procedure defined by validation team and repeatable across test sites.
Criteria measured with production software calibration for the active assistance mode used by customers.
uncertainties: Edge cases (narrow lanes, abrupt cut-ins) may still require stronger corrective action; those will be documented separately.
Behavior may vary depending on wheel/tire choice and road friction.

drafts.title: Help drivers find compatible fast chargers quickly and reliably
drafts.description: When planning long trips or navigating, the vehicle clearly shows fast chargers that are compatible with the car and prioritizes them so drivers spend minimal time verifying compatibility.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: On a variety of cross-country route-planning scenarios, at least 95% of charger suggestions presented by the vehicle's navigation are compatible with the vehicle's charging plug and charging profile, and users can identify compatibility status for a suggested charger within 3 seconds from the map or charging-details view in 95% of trials.
assumptions: A regularly updated charger database with connector and power information is available to the vehicle.
Compatibility matching includes connector type and minimum supported power levels.
Navigation UI presents compatibility status visually and in text.
uncertainties: Public charger data quality and third-party network reliability may cause occasional false-positives/negatives.
Interoperability agreements and roaming access across charging networks can impact real-world availability.

drafts.title: Make charging state visible at a glance from the charge port
drafts.description: When the vehicle is charging, the charge port light communicates status (charging, full, fault) clearly so users can tell the state without using the app or opening the car.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: From 3 meters and in daylight, users correctly identify charge port status (charging / complete / fault) within 3 seconds in at least 95% of trials using the port indicator alone; distinct and consistent color/flash patterns are used for each state.
assumptions: Port indicator uses visible color/flash patterns and is positioned for line-of-sight when the charger is connected.
Indicator brightness is sufficient for daylight visibility and dimmable for night to avoid glare.
uncertainties: Extreme glare or obstructions at the charge port (covers, aftermarket cages) may reduce visibility.
Color-blind users may require shape/flash-pattern redundancy; this should be validated in user testing.

drafts.title: Offer at least one configuration with a real-world range of 600 miles
drafts.description: Provide at least one powertrain configuration for the model line that delivers a real-world driving range of at least 600 miles on one tank or charge, so customers who prioritize long range can choose it.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: At least one official production configuration achieves >= 600 miles real-world range demonstrated on a standardized 600-mile mixed highway/city route without refueling/recharging in 95% of validation trials (or equivalent EPA highway combined test confirming >=600 miles where applicable).
assumptions: The 600-mile offering may be achieved via an ICE, a larger-fuel-tank hybrid, or a high-energy-density battery option depending on market and regulation.
Range claims are based on real-world validation runs and matched to the advertised configuration (tires, roof load, towing excluded).
uncertainties: Achieving 600 miles on a pure BEV platform within successor timelines is uncertain and depends on battery energy density progress or significantly larger pack sizes.
Regional emissions/efficiency regulations and market demand may influence which powertrains are offered.

drafts.title: Regulatory: Level 3 automated driving type approval request (Germany)
drafts.description: Customers request that the vehicle obtains type approval for Level 3 automated driving in Germany.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: This is a regulatory homologation request; product teams should track certification needs externally.
drafts.scope_reason: Request concerns type approval/regulation (homologation) which is outside product feature requirements; certification work is managed by regulatory/compliance teams.

drafts.title: Regulatory: CARB emission limits compliance request (US states)
drafts.description: Customers ask that the powertrain complies with CARB emission limits in all US states.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: This is a regulatory compliance request; product teams should refer to regulatory/certification processes.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulatory compliance request; out of scope for product-level customer-facing requirements.

drafts.title: Regulatory: UN R155 cybersecurity type approval request
drafts.description: Customers ask that the vehicle fulfils UN R155 cybersecurity type approval.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: This is a regulatory/certification request to be handled by compliance teams.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulatory/certification topic outside the product requirement scope.

drafts.title: Regulatory: EU battery passport compliance request
drafts.description: Customers ask that the vehicle's battery complies with the EU battery passport regulation.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: This is a regulatory data/transparency request; certification and data provision are handled by compliance teams.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulation/data-reporting requirement (battery passport) — out of scope for customer-facing product requirements.

drafts.acceptance_criterion: Engineering architecture specification request; treat as out of scope for customer-facing requirements and forward to architecture teams.
drafts.scope_reason: Technical architecture specification (800 V) — engineering detail outside customer-facing requirement scope.

drafts.acceptance_criterion: Onboard charger power rating is an engineering specification; capture as an engineering request for trade-off analysis.
drafts.scope_reason: Engineering specification (onboard charger kW) — out of scope for customer-facing requirements.

drafts.title: Engineering spec request: solid-state cells with 400 Wh/kg (out of scope)

drafts.acceptance_criterion: Battery cell chemistry and density are engineering/technology choices; capture for technology roadmap and not as direct customer-facing requirement.
drafts.scope_reason: Engineering/technology specification (cell chemistry and Wh/kg) — out of scope for customer-facing requirements.

drafts.title: Engineering spec request: 395 mm front brake discs (out of scope)

drafts.acceptance_criterion: Brake disc diameter is a hardware specification to be evaluated by engineering; not a customer-facing requirement.
drafts.scope_reason: Specific component dimension request — engineering detail outside customer-facing requirement scope.

drafts.description: Customers request that highway assist uses a lidar sensor from a named supplier.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Supplier selection is a procurement/engineering decision; log request but treat as out of scope for customer-facing requirements.
drafts.scope_reason: Request specifies supplier selection — procurement/engineering decision outside customer-facing requirement scope.
